Medium

1MediumCounterexample

In a Solow economy with depreciation δ=0.1\delta = 0.1δ=0.1, find steady-state consumption c∗=y∗−δk∗c^* = y^* - \delta k^*c∗=y∗−δk∗ for saving rates s=0.2s = 0.2s=0.2, s=0.4s = 0.4s=0.4, and s=0.8s = 0.8s=0.8.

Does eating more in the steady state always follow from saving more?

Verdict

The claim is false — at a saving rate of 0.80.80.8 steady-state consumption drops to 1.61.61.6, less than the 2.42.42.4 eaten at 0.40.40.4

  • A Country Cannot Grow on Machines Alone
Show solution

Counterexample and verification

  1. For s=0.2s = 0.2s=0.2: y∗=2y^* = 2y∗=2 and k∗=4k^* = 4k∗=4, so replacing worn machines costs δk∗=0.4\delta k^* = 0.4δk∗=0.4 and c∗=2−0.4=1.6c^* = 2 - 0.4 = 1.6c∗=2−0.4=1.6.

    For s=0.4s = 0.4s=0.4: y∗=4y^* = 4y∗=4, k∗=16k^* = 16k∗=16, replacement costs 1.61.61.6, and c∗=4−1.6=2.4c^* = 4 - 1.6 = 2.4c∗=4−1.6=2.4.

    Up to here, saving more does mean eating more.

  2. But at s=0.8s = 0.8s=0.8, y∗=8y^* = 8y∗=8 and k∗=64k^* = 64k∗=64, replacement alone eats 6.46.46.4, and c∗=8−6.4=1.6c^* = 8 - 6.4 = 1.6c∗=8−6.4=1.6 — back down again.

    Pile up too many machines and most of the output leaks into maintaining them.

    Steady-state consumption peaks at s=0.5s = 0.5s=0.5, where c∗=2.5c^* = 2.5c∗=2.5.

Hard

2Hard

A household with interest rate r=0.04r = 0.04r=0.04 and income y=4y = 4y=4 holds assets a=10a = 10a=10.

Find its optimal next-period assets for patience β=0.80\beta = 0.80β=0.80, 0.900.900.90, and 0.950.950.95, then find the smallest β\betaβ (on a two-decimal grid) at which this household stops running its assets down.

  • Where the Saving Rate Comes From
Show solution

  1. Reading the value-iteration policy at assets 101010: β=0.80\beta = 0.80β=0.80 gives a′=4a' = 4a′=4 (consumption 10.410.410.4), β=0.90\beta = 0.90β=0.90 gives a′=7a' = 7a′=7 (consumption 7.47.47.4), and β=0.95\beta = 0.95β=0.95 gives a′=9a' = 9a′=9 (consumption 5.45.45.4). Resources are 14.414.414.4 in all three cases — each step of patience moves food from today's plate to tomorrow's storehouse.

  2. Not running assets down requires a′≥10a' \ge 10a′≥10.

    At β=0.95\beta = 0.95β=0.95, a′=9a' = 9a′=9 still falls one step short; at β=0.96\beta = 0.96β=0.96, a′=10a' = 10a′=10 (consumption 4.44.44.4) holds the line for the first time.

    The border sits near where β(1+r)=1\beta (1 + r) = 1β(1+r)=1, that is β=1/1.04≈0.9615\beta = 1 / 1.04 \approx 0.9615β=1/1.04≈0.9615: the point where patience, grossed up by the interest rate, exactly balances.
